A_target.statement:
Let $f: \R^n \to \hointl {-\infty} \infty$ be [[Definition:Closed Convex Function|closed]] and [[Definition:Convex Real Function|convex]].
Let:
:$\displaystyle \map {f^*} y = \sup_x \paren {\innerprod y x - \map f x}$
be its [[Definition:Legendre-Fenchel Transform|Legendre-Fenchel transform]].
Then:
:$f^{**} = f$

B_source.statement:
Let $f$ be [[Definition:Closed Convex Function|closed]] and [[Definition:Convex Real Function|convex]].
Then $f$ is the [[Definition:Supremum of Mapping|supremum]] of the [[Definition:Affine Function|affine functions]] lying below it.

substitutions.an affine minorant of the function: a pair consisting of a slope and an intercept
substitutions.the family of all affine minorants: the transform, recording the least intercept for each slope
substitutions.the supremum over minorants: the double transform, reconstructing the function

derived.the transform of the function: the function evaluated on slopes rather than points
derived.applying the transform twice: recovery of the original function, so the transform is an involution

object_map.reformulation: Record the function by its family of affine minorants, indexing by slope rather than by argument.

validity_conditions: Closedness and convexity are exactly what guarantee the function is the supremum of its affine minorants; without them the double transform gives the closed convex hull instead.
For each slope the set of admissible intercepts is bounded above, so recording the least one loses nothing and the transform is well defined.
The transform exchanges the roles of point and slope, which is why it converts a strictly convex function into another and swaps differentiability with strict convexity.
proof_plan:
By the source result:
:$\displaystyle \map f x = \sup \set {\innerprod y x - c: \innerprod y \cdot - c \le f}$

For each slope $y$, the least intercept $c$ making $\innerprod y \cdot - c$ a minorant of $f$ is:
:$\displaystyle c = \sup_x \paren {\innerprod y x - \map f x}$

Hence:
:$\displaystyle \map f x = \sup_y \paren {\innerprod y x - \map {f^*} y} = \map {f^{**} } x$
using closed convexity for the first equality.
{{qed}}
